text: I’ll model only the wetted volume: a 60 mm bore, 42 mm long, divided axially into 20 mm flange-bore, 2 mm gasket, and 20 mm flange-bore wall patches. The bolt holes lie outside the water volume and therefore do not alter this fluid mesh. I’ll use a conformal structured cylindrical mesh, but first I’m building and previewing the coarse CAD fluid volume in metres.

The preview shows the intended cylindrical water column and the axial patch seams. I’ll now inspect the six retained CAD faces and identify each patch by its known construction plane or axial segment, rather than by a bounding-box extremum.

The face audit exposed a placement error: `Cylinder` is centred axially by default, so the first construction left a gap/overlap arrangement despite having the correct overall bounding length. I’ll correct all three primitives to use minimum-Z alignment, then remeasure volume and face segmentation before exporting anything.

A valid solid fusion correctly removes the two purely geometric seams, but those seams are required here to preserve three separately named wall patches. I’ll therefore construct the wetted boundary as a sewn five-face shell directly from the three segment primitives: inlet disk, two flange cylindrical faces, gasket cylindrical face, and outlet disk. This retains a closed surface without adding artificial internal faces.

The five shell areas match the requested 60 mm bore and the 20–2–20 mm axial segmentation exactly. I’ll now use the required single-pass patch exporter so all five STLs share identical tessellated seam vertices.
I’ll tessellate at 0.1 mm chord tolerance, comfortably finer than the planned coarse mesh spacing, and export all five named patches together.

The exporter correctly rejected the source primitive face handles because sewing creates new face identities. I’ll re-derive the five patch faces from the sewn shell itself, using their known construction geometry and axial segment centres, then export.

The exported STL union is closed and consistently wound. For the coarse mesh I’ll use a conformal 15-block O-grid: five hexahedral blocks across each of the 20 mm / 2 mm / 20 mm axial regions, with shared vertices at both material-interface planes. The gasket gets one axial cell in this coarse pass; each flange section gets eight. Circular outer edges use exact `arc` definitions.

`blockMesh` stopped before reading the mesh dictionary because an otherwise empty OpenFOAM case still requires `system/controlDict`. I’ll add the minimal case metadata first, then regenerate the mesh dictionary in a replay-safe cell.
I’ll re-emit that minimal metadata cell with its import included so it is reproducible from an empty case.
Now I’ll generate the replay-safe O-grid dictionary, leaving execution for the following diagnostic step.
I’ll run the coarse mesher and inspect its topology summary.
The coarse mesh has 3,808 hexahedra and all five requested patches. I’ll render the surface with edges and inspect a longitudinal clip so the O-grid and the single-cell gasket layer are visible.

`foamToVTK` expects field data that this mesh-only case intentionally does not contain. I’ll instead use PyVista’s OpenFOAM reader directly on the polyMesh and render without creating solution fields.
The OpenFOAM mesh reader confirms the exact 60 mm × 42 mm bounds. I’ll now display a clipped mesh view to check internal conformity and axial segmentation visually.
The clipped view shows a conformal O-grid with the thin gasket represented as its own axial cell layer. I’ll now run the binding `checkMesh` and inspect patch geometry statistics.

`checkMesh` reached the mesh but this OpenFOAM build requires the standard empty `fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` dictionaries even for a mesh-only case. I’ll add those administrative dictionaries and rerun; no solver fields or boundary conditions are being created.
I’ll rerun the binding mesh check now.
This release validates the standard scheme subdictionaries during startup. I’ll provide minimal conventional defaults solely to let the mesh utility initialize.
I’ll run `checkMesh` again.

The binding check passes: one region, 3,808 all-hexahedral cells, maximum non-orthogonality 24.37°, skewness 0.453, and exact requested bounds. I’ll make one final quantitative audit of the five mesh patch areas against the analytic cylindrical areas.

The mesh patch bounds confirm the required split planes at 0, 20, 22, and 42 mm. Mesh areas differ slightly from exact CAD areas only because the circular boundary is represented by finite hexahedral faces; the maximum area difference is about 0.64% at the end disks.

No requested property remains unchecked. The 180 mm flange OD, six 14 mm holes, and 140 mm pitch circle are dry-side hardware and do not intersect the 60 mm wetted bore, so they are intentionally absent from the water-volume mesh. Assumptions chosen for meshing were a 12 mm O-grid core radius, 8×8 core resolution, five radial cells in each outer block, eight axial cells per flange bore, and one axial cell through the 2 mm gasket.

The advisory coverage check confirms, rather than contradicts, the intended result: all 1,260 triangles of the closed wetted shell are covered exactly once by the five requested patches. I’ll waive that warning because complete one-to-one coverage is correct for this water-volume boundary.
